title: Number above a value from a cumulative frequency
source: Theory IGCSE-20.2 Quick check 1; total minus cumulative frequency
stem: A cumulative frequency diagram for the masses of {N|int} students shows that {c|int} students have a mass of {v|int} kg or less. How many of the students have a mass of more than {v|int} kg?

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: Subtract the cumulative frequency from the total: \({N|int}-{c|int}\).
steps.note: Cumulative frequency counts the values up to and including the reading.

steps.name: K
steps.note: Evaluate.

contexts.note: Includes the original 120 students with 84 at 50 kg or less, 36 more than 50 kg

title: Cumulative frequency at which the upper quartile is read
source: Theory IGCSE-20.2 Quick check 2; three quarters of the total
stem: A cumulative frequency curve is drawn for {n|int} values. At what cumulative frequency should the upper quartile be read?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The upper quartile is read at \(\dfrac{3}{4}\times{n|int}={A|int}\).
steps.note: Upper quartile at three quarters of the total frequency.

contexts.note: Includes the original 160 values, read at 120

title: Interquartile range from two readings
source: Theory IGCSE-20.2 Quick check 3; upper quartile minus lower quartile
stem: From a cumulative frequency curve, the lower quartile is {L|int} cm and the upper quartile is {U|int} cm. Find the interquartile range.

steps.name: R
steps.text_tex: Interquartile range \(={U|int}-{L|int}={i|int}\) cm
steps.note: Upper quartile minus lower quartile.

contexts.note: Includes the original quartiles 23 cm and 41 cm, interquartile range 18 cm

title: Cumulative frequency diagram for the heights of 200 plants

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The table shows some information about the heights of 200 plants.

Height (\(h\) cm)Cumulative frequency
\(h\le 30\)6
\(h\le 40\)42
\(h\le 50\)76
\(h\le 60\)170
\(h\le 70\)190
\(h\le 80\)200

(a) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram to show this information.

[3]

(b) Find an estimate of the 75th percentile. [1]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: (a) Plot the points at the correct heights \(h=30,40,50,60,70,80\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for correct horizontal placement for 6 plots.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (a) Plot them at the correct cumulative frequencies \(6, 42, 76, 170, 190, 200\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for correct vertical placement for 6 plots.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (a) Join the points with a smooth increasing curve or polygon, starting from \((20, 0)\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1FT dep on at least B1 for reasonable increasing curve or polygon through their 6 points. If 0 scored, SC1FT for 5 out of 6 points correctly plotted. A correct curve goes through [(20, 0)], (30, 6), (40, 42), (50, 76), (60, 170), (70, 190) and (80, 200).

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (b) Read the height at a cumulative frequency of \(0.75\times200=150\) (about 58 cm on a polygon through the points).
steps.note: Official MS: reading at 150 FT their increasing curve, 1 mark.

title: Cumulative frequency of car speeds, and the mean and histogram heights for truck masses

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
(a) The cumulative frequency table shows information about the speed of each of 200 cars as they pass a speed camera.

Speed (\(v\) km/h)Cumulative frequency
\(v\le 70\)12
\(v\le 80\)46
\(v\le 90\)115
\(v\le 95\)155
\(v\le 100\)177
\(v\le 120\)200

(i) On the grid, draw the cumulative frequency diagram.

[3]

(ii) Use your cumulative frequency diagram to find an estimate of

(a) the median [1]

(b) the interquartile range [2]

(c) the number of cars with a speed greater than 110 km/h. [2]

(b) The frequency table shows information about the mass of each of 50 trucks.

Mass (\(m\) kg)Frequency
\(2000\lt m\le 2600\)12
\(2600\lt m\le 3500\)15
\(3500\lt m\le 5000\)16
\(5000\lt m\le 5700\)7

(i) Calculate an estimate for the mean mass of the trucks. [4]

(ii) In a histogram showing this information, the height of the first block is 6 cm.

Calculate the heights of the remaining three blocks.

Height of block for \(2600\lt m\le 3500\) = …… cm

Height of block for \(3500\lt m\le 5000\) = …… cm

Height of block for \(5000\lt m\le 5700\) = …… cm [3]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: (a)(i) Plot the points at the correct speeds \(v=70,80,90,95,100,120\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for correct horizontal placement for 6 plots.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (a)(i) Plot them at the correct cumulative frequencies \(12, 46, 115, 155, 177, 200\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for correct vertical placement for 6 plots.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (a)(i) Join the points with a smooth increasing curve.
steps.note: Official MS: B1 dep on at least B1 for reasonable increasing curve through their 6 points. If 0 scored, SC1 for 4 out of 6 points correctly plotted.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (a)(ii)(a) Median: read at a cumulative frequency of 100, about 88 km/h.
steps.note: Official MS: 87 to 89.5, 1 mark.

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (a)(ii)(b) Lower quartile read at 50 (about 81 km/h) and upper quartile read at 150 (about 94 km/h), so the interquartile range is about 13 km/h.
steps.note: Official MS: 12.5 to 14, 2 marks; B1 for [LQ =] 80.5 to 81.5 or [UQ =] 94 to 94.5.

steps.name: s6
steps.text_tex: (a)(ii)(c) Read the cumulative frequency at 110 km/h from the diagram and subtract it from 200, giving a whole number. For reference only: on a polygon through the points the cumulative frequency at 110 is about 188–189, so about 11–12 cars.
steps.note: Official MS: strict FT, 200 – their cumul freq reading from their graph at 110 given to nearest integer, 2 marks; B1FT for correct cumul freq at 110 seen or for non-integer answer.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for midpoints soi.

steps.name: s8
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for use of Σfx where x is in the correct interval including boundaries.

steps.name: s9
steps.note: Official MS: M1 (dep on 2nd M1) for Σfx ÷ 50.

steps.name: s10
steps.note: Official MS: 3576, 4 marks.

steps.name: s11
steps.text_tex: (b)(ii) The first block has frequency density \(\dfrac{12}{600}=0.02\) and height 6 cm, so a frequency density of 1 is shown by \(300\) cm. Block for \(2600\lt m\le 3500\): \(\dfrac{15}{900}\times300=5\) cm.
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for each. If 0 scored, SC1 for 3 frequency densities 12/600, 15/900, 16/1500, 7/700 seen oe to 3sf or better, or multiplier 3 or 300.

steps.name: s12
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 3.2.

steps.name: s13
steps.text_tex: (b)(ii) Block for \(5000\lt m\le 5700\): \(\dfrac{7}{700}\times300=3\) cm.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 3.
